comparisons.peer_topic: Other Income (Expense), Net Composition and Results
comparisons.peer_summary: Other income (expense), net totaled $181 million in 2024, down from $197 million in 2023, primarily due to decreased interest income from lower short-term investment balances; this line item is primarily comprised of interest income from short-term investments, changes in valuation of equity investments, and foreign currency transaction gains and losses.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and AMD disclose the specific components comprising their 'Other income (expense), net' line item, with significant overlap in interest income, investment gains/losses, and foreign currency impacts. AVGO explicitly lists interest income, gains/losses on investments, and foreign currency remeasurement. AMD mirrors this structure, citing interest income from short-term investments, changes in valuation of equity investments, and foreign currency transaction gains/losses. A key difference is that AVGO groups these under a general 'miscellaneous' heading, while AMD quantifies the total net amount ($181 million in 2024) and attributes the year-over-year decrease specifically to lower short-term investment balances.

Other income (expense), net is primarily comprised of interest income from short-term investments, changes in valuation of equity investments and foreign currency transaction gains and losses.
The change was primarily due to a decrease in interest income from lower balances held in short-term investments compared to the prior year.

comparisons.peer_summary: In 2024, the company recognized net gains on equity investments of $242 million, primarily driven by $460 million in gains from its marketable equity investment portfolio, largely resulting from the sale of its interest in Astera Labs.
comparisons.comparison: While AVGO discloses the broad composition of 'Other income (expense), net' including investment gains, INTC provides granular detail on specific realized gains within that broader category, specifically from the sale of equity interests. AVGO's definition includes 'gains and losses on investments' generally. INTC highlights that in 2024 it recognized net gains on equity investments of $242 million, largely driven by $460 million in gains from the sale of its interest in Astera Labs. This illustrates how the 'gains on investments' component cited by AVGO manifests in INTC's filings as significant realized gains from divestitures.

comparisons.peer_topic: Other Net Income Components and Drivers
comparisons.peer_summary: Other, net includes realized or unrealized gains/losses from investments in non-affiliated entities and foreign currency impacts, with changes in fiscal year 2024 driven by valuation changes in those investments.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and NVDA define their 'Other income/expense, net' by including components related to investments and foreign currency. AVGO includes 'gains and losses on investments' and 'foreign currency remeasurement.' NVDA's 'Other, net' consists of 'realized or unrealized gains and losses from investments in non-affiliated entities' and 'impact of changes in foreign currency rates.' NVDA provides additional specificity by noting that fiscal year 2024 changes were driven by 'changes in value from our non-affiliated investments,' whereas AVGO's disclosure is more descriptive of the category list without attributing the 2024 variance to a single driver in the definition sentence.

Change in Other, net, compared to fiscal year 2023 was driven by changes in value from our non-affiliated investments.

comparisons.peer_summary: Fiscal 2024 interest and dividend income increased due to higher interest rates and balances on interest-bearing securities, while net gains on other investments were primarily driven by QSI non-marketable equity investments.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and QCOM report on 'other' income streams that include interest income and investment gains, though QCOM uses the label 'Investment and other income, net.' AVGO includes 'interest income' and 'gains on investments' in its 'Other income (expense), net.' QCOM's disclosure specifies that its increase in this category was due to 'higher interest rates earned on higher balances of interest-bearing securities' and net gains on 'non-marketable equity investments.' Similar to AMD and INTC, QCOM's disclosure highlights the driver of interest income (rates/balances), a component also present in AVGO's definition.
